title: Outbound Investment Security Program - Frequently Asked Questions
date_evidence: These questions and answers issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury provide general information to assist the public in understanding and complying with 31 CFR part 850 (the Outbound Rules); Executive Order 14105 issued by President Biden on August 9, 2023; Transactions with a completion date on or after January 2, 2025, are subject to the Outbound Rules
key_claim: The Outbound Investment Security Program implements Executive Order 14105 (issued 9 August 2023); the Outbound Rules (31 CFR part 850) took effect for transactions completed on or after 2 January 2025, imposing prohibitions and notification requirements on US persons' investments into countries of concern in semiconductors and microelectronics, quantum information technologies and certain artificial intelligence systems.
notes: Tier 1 primary instrument (the US OISP itself). Living FAQ page - is_evergreen; foundational dates (EO 14105 09/08/2023; effective 02/01/2025) read verbatim from the page.

title: Global Investment Trends Monitor, No. 50
date_evidence: Global Investment Trends Monitor, No. 50 (UNCTAD/DIAE/IA/INF/2026/1) - 20 Jan 2026
key_claim: Global FDI rose 14% in 2025 to USD 1.6 trillion, but more than USD 140 billion of the increase came from conduit flows through global financial centres - stripping those out, FDI rose only about 5%; flows to developed economies jumped 43% to USD 728 billion (EU +56%) while flows to developing economies fell 2% to USD 877 billion; data centres accounted for more than one fifth of global greenfield project values (announced investment exceeding USD 270 billion).
notes: Tier 1 primary data; supplies macro context and the strongest counter-evidence (capital is still flowing, FDI rebounded).

title: US reciprocal trade deals built to push America's trade partners away from China
key_claim: As of 22 May 2026, nine Agreements on Reciprocal Trade (ARTs) have been signed; among seven core exclusionary mechanisms, an 'investment security' clause requires partner countries to establish mechanisms for reviewing inbound and in some cases outbound investment based on national security risks (drawing on FIRRMA logic) to screen Chinese capital and technology-acquisition routes; China's share of US goods imports fell from 22% before the 2018-19 trade war to 9% by end-2025.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank; key evidence that outbound/inbound screening is being templated into US bilateral trade agreements - the propagation mechanism.

title: China Introduces New Outbound Investment Laws to Prevent U.S. Decoupling
key_claim: On 1 June 2026 China's State Council published new rules tightening control over outbound investment in key sectors including AI and national-security-related technologies, allowing Beijing to review planned deals on national-security grounds, ban cross-border data and technology transfers, extend scope to individual retail investors, punish foreign firms whose home countries restrict Chinese investment, and force the unwinding of completed overseas transactions; the piece argues US tools remain siloed across agencies, with BIS still roughly ten times larger than its Chinese counterpart.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank; evidence that the instrument has gone bilateral/mirror - China now runs its own outbound-screening regime.

title: China Tightens Outbound Investment Rules in US Tech Rivalry
date_evidence: China Tightens Outbound Investment Rules in US Tech Rivalry - Bloomberg ... 2026-06-01
key_claim: China's State Council moved on 1 June 2026 to tighten oversight of outbound investment on security grounds amid the US technology rivalry.
notes: Tier 3 journalism; corroborates the China outbound-rules development (paywalled body; title/date confirmed via search and corroborated by FDD).

title: Why US-China Decoupling Isn't Happening
key_claim: Robin Hu argues each round of tariffs, export controls and investment screening has been accompanied by more of the investments that cement the Sino-American economic relationship; restrictions meant to bifurcate the global economy accelerate adaptation that makes the system more resilient and harder to control unilaterally - so 'decoupling' describes a world that does not exist.
verbatim_quote: each round of tariffs, export controls, and investment screening has been accompanied by more of the investments that cement the Sino-American economic relationship
notes: Tier 3 quality commentary; the core counter-argument (screening is not producing decoupling). Lede page-verified; remainder paywalled.

publisher: Baker McKenzie (Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog)
title: President Trump Signs COINS Act Codifying and Expanding Outbound Investment Regulations
date_evidence: January 14, 2026 / By Terence Gilroy (US), Alexandre (Alex) Lamy (US) and Elliot Hecht (US)
key_claim: On 18 December 2025 President Trump signed the FY2026 NDAA, whose Title LXXXV is a revised Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security (COINS) Act; it codifies the OISP (effective 2 January 2025) and expands countries of concern from China (with Hong Kong and Macau) to add Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela, adds hypersonic systems and high-performance computing and supercomputing to covered technologies, authorises USD 150 million a year for the program (versus roughly USD 45 million for CFIUS in FY2025), and requires implementing regulations no later than 450 days after enactment (around March 2027).
notes: Tier 4 practitioner alert; authoritative mechanics of the COINS Act (corroborated across multiple law firms and the CRS product IF12629).
